validity.recommendation: keep as operating; no existence/classification/duplicate issue -- narrower spec/attribution defects filed separately below
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED independent of GEM/wiki, on primary sources: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America, LLC (NGPL) filed FERC Docket CP16-488 on 2016-08-01 for its 'Gulf Coast Expansion Project' (Federal Register 2016-19752, published 2016-08-18: new compressor station + 4,000-ft/30-in lateral in Cass County TX, abandonment of compression at Compressor Station 301 in Wharton County TX, 460,000 Dth/d, $69,399,000 for that specific certificate component). EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently carries the same docket as 'NGPL Gulf Coast Southbound Phase I' (Completed 2018-10-04, Project Type 'Reversal', $149M total, 460 MMcf/d). Kinder Morgan's own project page (Wayback 2018-07-13) describes 'the first phase of the project ... currently under construction ... designed to transport 460,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) ... from NGPL's interstate pipeline interconnects in Illinois, Arkansas and Texas ... anticipated to be fully in service by the fourth quarter of 2018.' Three independent organizations (FERC/Federal Register, EIA, Kinder Morgan) describe the same project with matching capacity, matching docket, and consistent geography. CLASSIFICATION correct: Fuel=Gas, an interstate FERC Natural Gas Act section 7 pipeline expansion, confirmed by all three sources. DUPLICATE CHECK: cross-checked against the 45-pipeline US-gas roster -- P2039 (Phase I, CP16-488, 2018 in-service, 460 MMcf/d) is genuinely distinct from P2541 (Phase II, CP19-99, 2021 in-service, +300 MMcf/d), P2495 (134th Street Lateral, CP20-14, an unrelated NGPL/NIPSCO interconnect lateral in IL/IN), and P0222 (the NGPL system-level row) -- no misclassification, relabeling, or duplication found. Two genuine defects are filed separately below (EndState/Province geography error, unsupported StartYear1, and a SegmentCost scope caveat).

validity.recommendation: correct EndState/Province from 'Louisiana' to 'Texas' -- the sheet's own EndLocation (Agua Dulce Hub) is itself in Texas, so the state cell contradicts its own row
validity.researcher_notes: Agua Dulce Hub, the sheet's recorded EndLocation, is a well-known gas hub near Corpus Christi, TEXAS -- not Louisiana. EIA's workbook independently states End_State=TX for this exact project (Beg_State=IL). FERC's Notice of Application (2016-19752) describes the certificated facilities entirely within Cass County, TX and Wharton County, TX, delivering to 'an existing delivery point and a new delivery point in the South Texas Gulf Coast area.' Both an authoritative US-government dataset and a primary federal regulatory filing place the delivery end of Phase I in Texas. NOTE: RBN Energy's tracker page for the sibling Phase II project (which lists Phase I's 'Base Capacity' alongside Phase II's own increment) ALSO states 'Destination: Agua Dulce Hub, LA' -- i.e. the same Louisiana error appears to be a shared/propagated mistake across at least one other source, not independent corroboration for 'Louisiana'. EIA + the FERC filing are the more authoritative, county-specific, tie-breaking sources; recommend Texas.

validity.recommendation: clear/blank StartYear1='2017' -- no source found supports a 2017 partial in-service date; StartYear2='2018' is well supported and should stay
validity.researcher_notes: The certificate timeline makes a 2017 in-service date implausible: NGPL's application was filed 2016-08-01 (FERC CP16-488, Federal Register 2016-19752), FERC did not issue its Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review until 2017-03-17, and every source that gives an in-service date -- EIA (Year In Service Date 2018, Completed Date 2018-10-04), Kinder Morgan's own July-2018 project page ('anticipated to be fully in service by the fourth quarter of 2018'), and RBN Energy's 2023 tracker snapshot -- points to 2018, none to 2017. No news release, FERC order, or corporate disclosure found placing any partial/phased in-service milestone in 2017. Recommend blanking StartYear1 rather than guessing a month; StartYear2=2018 is confirmed separately in the Start [ref] fill below.

validity.recommendation: SegmentCost=$149,000,000 (EIA's Phase-I-scoped total) is the best available figure, but flag the scope gap against the $69.4M FERC certificate-level figure for future verification -- do not treat the two as contradictory without more research
validity.researcher_notes: EIA's workbook records Cost (millions)=149 for the whole 'NGPL Gulf Coast Southbound Phase I' project line tied to Docket CP16-488. However, the actual Federal Register Notice of Application for that same docket states 'Total cost of the project is $69,399,000' (~$69.4M) for the specific facilities described (one new compressor station + a 4,000-ft/30-in lateral in Cass County TX + abandonment of compression in Wharton County TX). Working hypothesis, not fully resolved: Kinder Morgan's own project description describes Phase I as spanning interconnects/work across Illinois, Arkansas AND Texas (a broader multi-component build), while the one FERC Section 7 certificate application found covers only the Texas compression/lateral component -- i.e. EIA's $149M may aggregate more construction than the single certificate this session located. No second FERC docket was found to account for the remaining ~$80M (FERC eLibrary's docket-sheet UI is JS-rendered and not scriptable via curl). Recommend keeping EIA's $149M as the segment-level figure (tier=medium, single strong government source) while flagging the $69.4M certificate-level figure as documented context for a future researcher with FERC eLibrary access to reconcile.

Separately, Kinder Morgan's own asset page hosts the project under its 'Natural Gas Pipelines' business segment, and RBN Energy's tracker page states 'Operator: Kinder Morgan' -- reflecting that Kinder Morgan is NGPL's commercial manager/ultimate operator at the parent level (KMI's FY2021 10-K: 'We and Brookfield now each hold a 37.5% interest in NGPL Holdings', implying ArcLight Capital Partners holds the remaining 25%). This is a legitimate convention difference (legal FERC-certificated entity vs. commercial parent-manager), not a contradiction requiring correction -- see the P0222 cross_row_lead below, where the operators/owners tab's Owner2/Owner3 percentages for Brookfield/ArcLight appear transposed relative to the 10-K's stated split.
